name: Centrism
summary: Centrism is a position between left and right that favours moderate, gradual and pragmatic reform. Its best-documented strands are Third Way and radical centrism, which accept market economies while keeping a liberal welfare state, and stress opportunity with responsibility. It has no fixed program, so many policy answers are inferences.
scope: Mainstream Western centrism as documented in Third Way politics (Giddens, Blair, Clinton, Schroeder) and radical centrism (Satin, Halstead and Lind, Avlon). Excludes parties merely labelled centrist, centrist populism and agrarian or Christian-democratic variants. As a positional label rather than a program, many answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Pragmatism, rejection of left-right labels, market-based solutions with oversight.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Radical centrists favour market-based solutions with strong oversight in the public interest, so neither side is taken outright.

public-ownership.rationale: Third Way centrism accepts competitive markets and public-private partnerships rather than broad nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Third Way figures cut some taxes to attract investment, while other centrists accept moderate redistribution; adherents are split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale turns on whether regulation should be tighter than now, or on replacing corporations instead of regulating them, and the statement now asks whether corporations should face strict government regulation.

reviewHistory.rationale: Strong oversight is favoured alongside market solutions, so tighter regulation is a case-by-case question.

cut-welfare.rationale: Third Way reform favours workfare and a hand-up rather than cutting welfare outright.

strong-leader.rationale: Radical centrists want grounded movements and institutional reform rather than a single charismatic leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Centrists support a liberal welfare state and institutional reform, and reject abolishing the state.

traditional-family.rationale: Clinton stressed family and parental responsibility, yet social liberal centrists are less traditional; split.

gradual-change.rationale: Centrists favour gradual change and prioritise prudence in institutional reform.

free-trade.rationale: The Third Way accepts global economic integration and works to attract investment within it.

limit-growth.rationale: Third Way centrism prizes growth and the revenue it generates.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmental protection is a Third Way theme but drastic action is not defining; split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Centrists favour gradual, prudent reform over revolutionary change.

experts-over-public.rationale: Evidence-based policy appeals to centrists, but they also want democratic legitimacy; split.

central-planning.rationale: Third Way accepts competitive markets as the main engine of wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Third Way stresses work and responsibility rather than unconditional payments, though some radical centrists back it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Markets are the main engine of wealth, with state action where markets fail.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Centrism rejects abolishing the market economy.

one-party-rule.rationale: Centrism operates within plural party democracy.

democracy-best.rationale: Clinton's New Covenant stresses democratic community and citizen involvement; centrism is rooted in plural democracy.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Centrism supports a liberal welfare state and public institutions.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Clinton frames the country as one community going up or down together, rejecting class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Third Way stresses equality of opportunity paired with personal responsibility.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights with responsibilities pairs them rather than ranking duties first.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Radical centrists reject ideology and left-right labels, favouring realism and pragmatism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Third Way relies on markets and opportunity, not distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Third Way accepts markets and competition as the engine of wealth.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Third Way accepts markets and private enterprise rather than seeing profit as exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Alien to centrism, which rejects class rule.

taxation-theft.rationale: Centrists support a liberal welfare state funded by taxes.

positive-liberty.rationale: Third Way and social liberalism link freedom with opportunity and social capital.

total-state.rationale: Centrism rejects total state direction of life.

school-vouchers.rationale: Radical centrists back school choice but other centrists oppose; split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Clinton stressed a balanced budget and criticised structural deficits; Third Way favours fiscal discipline.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Pragmatism favoured, but no fixed epistemological claim.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Clinton backed welfare reform with tough work requirements; Third Way favours workfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: Clinton described the nation as one community and praised employers sharing gains with workers.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Centrism sits within the liberal democratic mainstream, which treats people alike before the law.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Centrists keep a liberal welfare state and regulated markets, so confining government to defense, justice and property is rejected.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Centrists are split on how to classify settler states and offer no common position.

separated-powers.rationale: Centrism favours moderate, balanced institutions and gradual reform over concentrated power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Centrists favour gradual, democratic and pluralist reform and reject revolutionary vanguard politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Third Way centrists favour opportunity for all and welfare-to-work rather than first priority to the poor; adherents are split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Centrism is a liberal-democratic position that keeps a free press independent of government.

party-commands-army.rationale: Centrism rests on constitutional liberal democracy, in which the armed forces serve the state and not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Centrists are split between liberal-integrationist and more restrictive centre-right strands; no settled centrist position.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Centrism is documented as supporting European integration and global cooperation.

death-penalty.rationale: Adherents are split: Clinton supported the death penalty while many European centrists oppose it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Centrists in the liberal tradition hold that political freedoms should not be traded away for growth.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Centrists are split between nuclear independence and reliance on alliances; the label sets no position.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Third Way governments accepted market orthodoxy and gave central banks independence, as Blair did in 1997.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Centrism is a liberal-democratic position; a sacred ruler of divine descent is wholly outside it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Third Way centrists kept progressive taxation to fund opportunity and a liberal welfare state, though some accept simpler tax systems.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule of law and accountable government are basic to the liberal democracy centrists defend.

space-expansion.rationale: Centrism has no position on space; adherents are split and treat it as a budget priority at most.

leader-cult.rationale: Public worship of a leader as the embodiment of the nation conflicts with centrist liberal-democratic pluralism.

refugee-return.rationale: Not a centrist concern; positions vary by party.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pragmatic centrism favors cooperation within existing borders rather than ancestry-based unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Centrists are split between integration and pluralism; no defining position.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Centrists are split; some center-left strands favor quotas, others merit.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Third Way positions on globalisation favor open trade and market integration, which excludes closed economic blocs.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Centrism favors moderate, gradual and pragmatic reform, which rules out armed vanguards.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Centrism has no fixed line on curriculum; moderates split between national-centred and pluralist history.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Third Way centrism accepts market economies and holds that regulation and growth can manage their cycles.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The doctrine does not address this, and centrists are split between realist and anti-imperial views.

delink-world-market.rationale: Third Way centrists embrace globalization and trade integration, as Clinton's Georgetown remarks on engagement and trade show.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: A positional label with no stance on colonial borders; adherents are split, so neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Moderates split between preserving with context and removal; no centrist doctrine.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Centrists are split between equal-services framing and gendered-pattern framing.

paid-care-work.rationale: Adherents are split; Third Way favours support for carers but not a general wage for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations are not a centrist program item; moderates are split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Third Way accepts open markets while allowing security review, so there is no settled position.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Third Way and radical centrism accept the market economy and private property.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not part of the centrist program and moderates are split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Moderates are divided between intent-based and effects-based views; the label has no fixed position.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not a centrist program issue; moderates are split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: No centrist doctrine addresses foreign funding of NGOs; adherents are split between open-society liberalism and sovereignty concerns.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: Third Way and radical centrism accept market economies and so reject common ownership of the means of production.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Third Way politics favours public-private partnership and market mechanisms inside publicly funded services.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Third Way centrists embrace market economies as the source of growth and opportunity.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Accepting market economies and liberal welfare states, centrism rejects common-property communities as a model for society.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream Western centrism sits inside liberal democracy and accepts the historical record.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Centrism works within liberal democracy and pluralism, so suppressing opposition is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Third Way thinkers called for deepening democracy and civic participation, but this is not central to centrism.

assisted-dying.rationale: Centrists are split between autonomy and caution about safeguards.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Third Way and radical centrism define themselves as going beyond left and right by combining the best ideas of each.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents split between French-style secularism and liberal tolerance.

property-franchise.rationale: Centrism endorses broad democratic participation and equal opportunity, and a property franchise contradicts both.

racial-franchise.rationale: Centrism rests on liberal-democratic universal citizenship and equal rights, which excludes racial limits on the vote.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Centrism rests on liberal tolerance and freedom of religion, so it opposes legal limits on interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Centrism rejects discrimination against religious minorities, and moderate liberal values treat such boycotts as prejudice.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Moderate pluralist centrists favor a neutral state in matters of belief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Moderate reform-minded centrism rejects radical abolition of core state institutions.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Third Way allowed private providers within public services, while others keep essentials public, so adherents are split.

municipal-property.rationale: Third Way and radical centrism accept market economies and private ownership.

family-wage.rationale: Centrists emphasize making work pay but have no stated line on household-based wages.

online-anonymity.rationale: Adherents split between privacy and safety concerns; no doctrine addresses it.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Centrism takes no position on spiritual questions; adherents differ.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Third Way leaders such as Clinton defended humanitarian intervention abroad, as the Georgetown remarks on Kosovo show, so force beyond self-defence is accepted.

free-public-college.rationale: Centrists support opportunity through education but are split on tuition-free provision versus means-tested aid.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: Centrism has no fixed view on gendered differences in values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Centrists accept defence needs while backing arms control; the label sets no position.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Third Way governments (Clinton, Blair) expanded the EITC and working tax credits as "make work pay" policy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Centrism is defined by gradual, pragmatic reform within existing institutions, the opposite of smashing the state.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Centrists favour opportunity with responsibility, supporting targeted relief but resisting blanket cancellation; they split.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Centrism is a positional label with no view on religious truth; adherents are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Centrism seeks broad cross-class coalitions and a position between left and right, so a separate workers' party is not its approach.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Centrists favour balancing environmental and economic goals pragmatically rather than ranking one absolutely.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Third Way figures such as Clinton backed tougher sentencing while radical centrists favour evidence-based reform; no settled position.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Centrists accept unions and market flexibility; Third Way figures have taken both sides of the right-to-work debate, so no common stance is documented.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Third Way and radical-centre thinkers favour market-based and work-linked supports, but the sources do not endorse a full replacement of welfare; split.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Third Way reform favours workfare and a hand-up rather than cutting welfare outright. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: The doctrine does not address this, and centrists are split between realist and anti-imperial views. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

notes: Strands differ: Christian-democratic and centre-right variants lean more conservative, centre-left Third Way variants more social-democratic. Centrism is a positional label, so most answers are inferences.
